market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: India multilayer flexible packaging market: 6.8%/yr CAGR; polyethylene-based films projected ~42% share of material type in 2026. India baby diaper market: $1.83B (2025) to $3.18B by 2034 (6.37%/yr, 2026-2034); baby diapers dominate at 88.09% share (2025). India overall plastic packaging market: $22.44B (2025) to $26.89B by 2031 (3.06%/yr) — much slower than the hygiene-films sub-segment, indicating hygiene packaging is an above-market-growth niche.
exportGeographies: Oman (SPF exports, via sister entity Ecoplast)
market.domesticSlice: UFlex is India's largest multinational flexible packaging company, offering wicketed bags/handle films for baby and hygiene markets with strong export presence (North America, Europe, Africa, SE Asia, Middle East). Ecoplast Limited (listed, now merging with Kunal Plastics) posted FY26 revenue ₹221 Cr, PAT ₹12 Cr, ROE 11%, ROCE 14.4%.

structureFacts: India mandated a minimum 30% recycled content in PET bottles from April 2025, with a 60% target by 2029 — a regulatory tailwind directly relevant to PIR/PCR (Post-Industrial/Post-Consumer Recycled) plastic incorporation
Hygiene packaging films are a distinct high-barrier, high-spec sub-category within flexible packaging, requiring multilayer co-extrusion for moisture/microbial barrier performance

adoptionStructure.note: Hygiene/FMCG brand buyers prioritize barrier performance (moisture/microbial), softness/skin-safety compliance for baby/medical use, consistent multilayer coextrusion quality at high production speeds, and increasingly recycled-content credentials (PIR/PCR) to meet brand sustainability commitments and regulatory mandates.
